trust.title: Built with health workers, for rural Bangladesh
trust.body: Medbridge is not a video-call app with a medical theme. It is a path a community health worker walks with you — registering your record, taking your vitals, and staying in the loop after the doctor has replied.

privacy.title: Your records stay between your care team
privacy.body: Only the doctor and health worker looking after you can see your consultations, prescriptions, and diary entries. Nobody else.

chwBacked.title: A trained health worker is always in the loop
chwBacked.body: If you don't have a smartphone, your CHW carries the platform to you, records your vitals, and books the consultation on your behalf.

coverage.title: Serving rural unions and upazilas
coverage.body: Our partner health workers and clinics cover villages across Lakshmipur, Noakhali, Bhola, and Feni, with more districts joining.

faq.title: Common questions
faq.subtitle: If something else is on your mind, our contact page has more.

cost.a: Consultations are free for rural patients registered through a community health worker. You only pay for medicines at the pharmacy, the same as anywhere else.

noSmartphone.q: What if I don't have a smartphone?
noSmartphone.a: You don't need one. A community health worker visits your village, registers your record, takes your vitals, and relays the consultation for you on their device.

privacy.q: Who can see my health records?
privacy.a: Only the doctor and health worker directly involved in your care. Your information is never shared with anyone else, including other patients or providers.

emergency.a: Medbridge is not an emergency service. For a medical emergency, call your national emergency number or go to the nearest hospital directly. Critical vitals recorded on the platform do alert a doctor immediately, but this is not a substitute for emergency care.

howItWorks.metaDescription: How a Medbridge consultation runs, from a health worker visiting a village to medicine being dispensed.
howItWorks.title: From a village visit to medicine in hand
howItWorks.intro: Medbridge is not a video-call app with a medical theme. It is the whole path a rural patient takes — registration, triage, consultation, prescription, dispensing — with each step recorded so the next person in the chain is not guessing.

register.title: A health worker registers the patient
register.body: A community health worker (CHW) visits the village and creates the patient record on their phone. The system issues a permanent medical record number so every later visit, vital, and prescription attaches to the same person.

vitals.title: Vitals and symptoms are recorded on the spot
vitals.body: Temperature, blood pressure, pulse, and oxygen saturation go in alongside the complaint. The platform scores them against clinical thresholds and suggests a triage level — the health worker can override it, because they are the one in the room.

critical.title: Critical cases alert a doctor immediately
critical.body: When triage comes back CRITICAL, a doctor and the duty administrators are notified in the same instant the record is saved. Nothing waits in a queue for someone to notice it.

consultation.title: The consultation happens over secure chat
consultation.body: The doctor reviews the vitals, symptom history, and past consultations, then talks to the patient or the health worker in real time. Text works on the low-bandwidth connections rural clinics actually have — no video call to drop.

prescription.title: The doctor issues a prescription
prescription.body: Medicines are chosen from a catalogue with live stock levels, so a doctor does not prescribe something the pharmacy cannot supply. Once issued, a prescription cannot be edited — only cancelled with a reason, which stays on the record.

dispensing.title: The pharmacy dispenses and stock updates itself
dispensing.body: Handing over medicine records what was given and decrements inventory in one step. Partial dispensing is normal, so the prescription stays open until everything has been supplied. Crossing a stock threshold alerts the pharmacist automatically.

howItWorks.principlesTitle: Why it is built this way

bandwidth.title: Built for weak connections
bandwidth.body: Chat-first rather than video-first. A consultation completes over a 2G signal.

records.title: Records that cannot be quietly rewritten
records.body: Prescriptions are immutable, accounts are deactivated rather than deleted, and sensitive actions are written to an audit trail.

chw.title: The health worker is part of the system
chw.body: Patients without a smartphone are not locked out — a CHW carries the platform to them and stays in the loop afterwards.

howItWorks.readyBody: Patients can register directly. Doctors, health workers, and pharmacists are onboarded by an administrator.

chwsPage.title: Community health workers
chwsPage.subtitle: Trained health workers who register patients, record vitals, and arrange consultations across rural Bangladesh.
chwsPage.whatBody: Community Health Workers visit villages, register patients into Medbridge, measure vital signs, and schedule consultations with qualified doctors. They are the link between your village and the healthcare system.

contactPage.subtitle: Questions about a consultation, joining as a provider, or partnering with us — this is the place.
contactPage.emailBody: Best for account problems and provider applications.
contactPage.hoursBody: Clinical escalation runs around the clock — a CRITICAL triage alerts a doctor immediately, whatever the hour.
contactPage.emergencyBody: Medbridge is not an emergency service. For a medical emergency call your national emergency number or go to the nearest hospital.
contactPage.whereBody: Rural unions and upazilas served by our partner clinics and community health workers.
contactPage.joinBody: Provider accounts are created by an administrator so credentials can be verified before anyone sees a patient. Email us and we will take it from there.

diary.title: Health diary
diary.subtitle: A line a day. Your doctor reads this before your next consultation.
diary.nothingToday: Nothing written today. Even “same as yesterday” is useful — it is the gaps that make a pattern hard to read.
diary.emptyBody: Write down how you feel, what hurts, and whether you took your medicine. Over a few weeks it becomes the clearest picture of your health anyone has.
diary.whoCanSee1: The doctor and health worker looking after you. Nobody else.
diary.whoCanSee2: Say it plainly. There is no wrong way to describe how you feel.
diary.whoCanSee3: If something feels seriously wrong, do not wait for your next appointment — call for help.
diary.honestyNote: Missed doses are worth recording honestly. A doctor changing a medicine that was never taken is a worse outcome than admitting you forgot.
diary.deleteBody: The entry from {date} will be removed for good, including from your doctor's view of your diary.
diary.ownWordsPlaceholder: Slept better last night. The cough is still there in the mornings.
diary.tookMedicine: I took my medicine as prescribed today
diary.tookMedicineHint: Untick it if you missed a dose. Nobody is marking you on this.
diary.worseDanger: Feeling worse with pain that high is not something to sit on. Contact your health worker or the nearest facility today.
diary.noteRequired: Write a line about how you feel

visits.title: Field visits
visits.subtitle: Your round, house by house. Logging a visit is what turns coverage into a number.
visits.emptyBody: Nothing recorded in the last {days} days. Log a visit as you finish it — the details are easy to lose by evening.
visits.whyBody: A logged visit is the only proof a household was reached. Unlogged rounds do not show up in anyone’s coverage figures, including yours.
visits.removeBody: The visit to {name} on {date} will be deleted, and your coverage figures will drop by one. Any triage recorded during it stays.
visits.notesPlaceholder: Wound dressing changed, healing well. Family understands the medicine schedule.
visits.needsFollowUpHint: Counted as open until you log another visit to the same person.
visits.notHomeNote: Worth logging anyway — a household nobody can reach is exactly what the coverage figures need to show.
visits.travelWhole: Travel time has to be a whole number of minutes

urgencyNote.URGENT: Should be seen within a day or two.
urgencyNote.EMERGENCY: Every administrator is alerted the moment you send it.

medicines.searchPlaceholder: Search by brand or generic name…
medicines.lowStockHint: Showing medicines below their stock threshold. Search to reach any other item in the catalogue.
medicines.nothingMatchedBody: Try the generic name instead of the brand.
medicines.allHealthyBody: Nothing is below its threshold right now. Search to find a specific medicine.
medicines.retireHint: Unticking retires the medicine. Nothing is deleted — prescriptions that already reference it stay intact.
medicines.stockNotEditable: Stock quantity and threshold are not editable here — thresholds are fixed at creation and stock only moves through a recorded adjustment.
medicines.vRequired: Brand name, generic name, and strength are required
medicines.belowThreshold: New level {level} — below the threshold of {threshold}. A low-stock alert will go out.
medicines.addSubtitle: Creates the catalogue entry and its opening inventory record together.
medicines.thresholdHint: Alerts fire when stock drops below this
medicines.thresholdNote: The threshold can only be set now — later stock changes go through a recorded adjustment, which does not touch it.
medicines.alternativesHint: Pairs are symmetric — this medicine will also show up as an alternative to anything you list here, so a patient can find a substitute when the pharmacy runs out.
medicines.availableHint: Leave this on unless you are pre-loading something the pharmacy does not stock yet.
